### MOTION SUBMITTING LUMA’S POSITION REGARDING GENERA’S REQUEST FOR EXPEDITED APPROVAL OF EMERGENCY GENERATION CAPACITY SOLUTIONS

### TO THE HONORABLE PUERTO RICO ENERGY BUREAU:

**COME NOW LUMA Energy, LLC** (“ManagementCo”), and **LUMA Energy Servco, 
LLC** (“ServCo”) (jointly referred to as “LUMA”), through the undersigned counsel, and 
respectfully state and request the following:

1. On February 26, 2025, Genera PR, LLC ("Genera") filed with this Puerto Rico 
Energy Bureau of the Public Service Regulatory Board ("Energy Bureau") a document entitled 
*Request for Expedited Approval of Emergency Generation Capacity Solutions* (“Genera Request”) 
in which Genera seeks the Energy Bureau’s approval for Genera to enable the implementation of 
the following proposed options for temporary generation to “allow for critical maintenance to be 
performed on existing power plants while stabilizing the grid in the short term” and to “guarantee 
system stability while recovery projects are performed”: (a) installing additional Temporary 
Mobile Generators of approximately 800 MW for 18 months; (b) substituting damaged units with 
pre-owned but functional generating units; and (c) deploying generation barges to supplement the 
power supply. *See Genera Request,* ¶ 6 and WHEREFORE.

---

2. On February 27, 2025, this Energy Bureau issued a Resolution and Order 
(“February 27<sup>th</sup> Order) whereby it determined that it was LUMA’s responsibility, “as the system 
operator and energy dispatcher, to prepare and submit (supported by the necessary technical 
information) any request for additional generation within the framework of the adequacy of 
resources”. See February 27<sup>th</sup> Order, p.1. (Translation ours.) The Energy Bureau then granted 
LUMA until March 6, 2025, at 5:00pm to present its position on the Request and, specifically, “the 
need for additional temporary generation, and the capacity thereof, if any, in light of the findings 
of the Resource Adequacy Report”.  The Resource Adequacy Report refers to a report prepared by 
LUMA titled *Puerto Rico Electrical System Resource Adequacy Analysis Report* and submitted to 
the Energy Bureau on October 31, 2024, in Case No. NEPR-MI-2022, *In re: LUMA Resource 
Adequacy Study.* The Energy Bureau also ordered Genera to immediately provide LUMA with any 
information that the latter deems necessary to comply with the February 27<sup>th</sup> Order. Id.

# LUMA’s Position on Genera Request for Expedited Approval of Emergency Generation Capacity Solution

In accordance with the Resolution and Order (“R&O”) dated February 27, 2025, issued by the Puerto Rico 
Energy Bureau (“Energy Bureau”), LUMA was ordered to provide its position on Genera’s request for 
Expedited Approval of Emergency Generation Capacity Solutions, which includes:

1. Installing 800 megawatts of additional temporary mobile generators for 18 months

2. Substituting damaged units with pre-owned but functional generating units

3. Deploying generation barges to supplement the power supply.

In compliance with the February 27<sup>th</sup> R&O, LUMA has prepared this preliminary response. An assessment 
of individual project locations, interconnections and fuel supply requires additional analysis before full 
feasibility of any proposal can be determined.

#### Summary of LUMA’s Response

LUMA analyses the adequacy of the generation supply portfolio each year in the annual Resource 
Adequacy Report as part of its obligation under the Transmission and Distribution System Operation and 
Maintenance Agreement (“T&D OMA”). The past three annual reports have consistently shown that 
Puerto Rico has a generation supply deficit of between 700-850 MW. These assessments confirm the
fragility of the generation supply portfolio, which are further strained by the recent catastrophic failure of 
the Aguirre1 Power Plant (“Aguirre Unit 1”).

#### Background to Puerto Rico’s Resource Adequacy Deficiencies

LUMA first quantified Puerto Rico's generation inadequacies in the Systems Operations Principles Report 
(“SOP”) submitted to the Energy Bureau in December 2021. In the four years since that report, the only 
generation capacity added to the grid was the 26 MW of wind capacity at Punta Lima and 350 MW of TM 
2500 emergency generators. However, these incremental additions have been offset by reduced 
availability of existing units and increase in load over the past three years. Unless additional generation 
capacity is added to the grid, the situation will deteriorate further.

The Resource Adequacy picture in Puerto Rico can be visually seen in **Slide 1** of the attached Exhibit 2.  
The chart shows graphically which hours of the year the Puerto Rico grid has a reserve margin that is 
required under the System Operations Principles document approved by the Energy Bureau in the Spring 
of 2022. The chart shows that the available reserves in the evening hours are now below required levels 
for most of the year as evidenced by the red cells indicating capacity below recommended reserve levels. 
Black cells show the number of hours where there is not enough generation capacity, thus precipitating a 
load shed event.

Further evidence of the generation shortfall condition in Puerto Rico can be seen in **Slide 2** which 
displays the 115 individual load shed (combination of generation shortfalls and under frequency) events 
which occurred in 2024. For perspective, the general industry Planning Standard for North American 
utilities is to have enough generation reserves to tolerate one single load shed event every ten years. This

---

##### RESPONSE TO FEBRUARY 27, RESOLUTION

##### NEPR-MI-2024-0005

means Puerto Ricans experience 1,150 times as many load shed events as the average electricity 
customer in North America.

LUMA has developed a set of analytical methods that predicts with reasonable accuracy the expected 
frequency and duration of manual load shed events from generation shortfalls in upcoming months. As 
reflected in the **Slide 3,** the actual number of load shed events experienced since July 2022 is consistent 
with the expected number of load shed events predicted by LUMA in its Resource Adequacy forecast.

The above reflects the immediate need for additional generation in order to meet customer demand and 
maintain adequate generation reserves.

#### Impact of Catastrophic Failure of the Aguirre Unit 1 on the Outlook for Summer 2025

LUMA is completing a Resource Adequacy Summer Update focused on the risks of load shed for the 
upcoming summer and peak demand season. This update includes the potential impact of other 
unpredictable factors that could further worsen capacity deficiencies, such as additional plant 
unavailability, potential impacts of a Category 3 hurricane, or extended heat wave which would increase 
generation demand. LUMA’s analysis, which is expected to be published by the end of March 2025, 
preliminarily expects 90 generation shortfall events between May 1, 2025, and October 31, 2025, as 
shown in **Slide 4,** a significant increase when compared to 20 load shed events that occurred in the same 
period in 2024. This outcome is heavily impacted by the recent forced outage at Aguirre Unit 1. However, 
the unavailability of Aguirre Unit 1 is not the only contributing factor. As shown in **slide 5,** the number of 
generation shortfall events would be reduced from approximately 90 to 60 if Aguirre Unit 1 were available.

When Under-Frequency Load Sheds (“UFLS”) are included (based on the recent trend of approximately 
70 UFLSs per year), the preliminary results from this update suggests that approximately 125 load sheds 
can be expected to occur between May and October 2025, or approximately 20 per month, double the 
incidence of load shed events in 2024.

Finally, LUMA’s preliminary analysis of generation supply suggests that several factors could further 
worsen these estimates. **Slide 6** shows the potential impact of a Category 3 Hurricane, an extended 
summer heat wave, or a 1-month heat wave which would increase generation demand, or the loss of 
another baseload generating plant for the summer. These sensitivities show that any of these events 
would add approximately 30 more load shed events over the same 6-month period.

#### Impact to Requested Retirements / Replacement Projects

Another important consideration related to the generation shortfall condition and Genera’s proposal to add 
800 MW is the benefits that the addition of generation capacity could have on enabling Genera to 
proceed with its plan to replace existing peakers as well as adding battery capacity.

As System Operator, LUMA has the responsibility to ensure planned outage schedules are made taking 
into account the need to meet customer demand and maintain sufficient reserves to operate reliably, 
within existing and unavoidable constraints. In this context, LUMA rejected Genera’s initial schedule of 
peaker replacements and Battery Energy Storage System (“BESS”) additions because most of the site 
locations for the proposed additions would require existing generation capacity to be taken out of service, 
before the replacement facility could be constructed and operational. This proposed schedule would 
therefore have significantly increased load shed risks and would require operating the system outside of 
acceptable parameters. LUMA is currently working with Genera to explore other potential solutions to

---

##### RESPONSE TO FEBRUARY 27, RESOLUTION

##### NEPR-MI-2024-0005

scheduling these retirements and replacements in a way that minimizes the negative impact to electricity 
system reliability.

The addition of approximately 800 MW would enable Genera to continue with its unit replacement plans 
without putting at risk the operational stability or reliability of the system.

#### Overall Load Shed Benefits of Genera’s Proposed Generation Additions

In response to Genera's proposal, LUMA has analyzed the impact of adding emergency generation to the 
current load shed forecast. In **Slide 7,** LUMA shows the improvement of adding 800 MW, as well as 
smaller increments of adding 350 MW and 150 MW, for the summer of 2025. LUMA used the three 
scenarios to reflect the uncertainty of how much emergency generation Genera can be located and when 
it might be installed.

LUMA has not had the opportunity to review nor make any assessment of the schedule or technical 
challenges of locating and installing 800 MW of generation. This requires a thorough assessment of 
Genera’s proposal such as identifying and prioritizing locations, assessing site conditions, and performing 
system impact modeling. While some of this work can be sped up by leveraging previous efforts related to 
the Generation Stabilization effort conducted after Hurricane Fiona, such an assessment require a sizable 
workforce and budget to complete. LUMA looks forward to supporting Genera as it proceeds down this 
path of evaluating how to procure and then to install this additional generation.

**RE: LUMA’s Letter to Genera, re: PREB’s February 27, 2025, Resolution and Order Regarding** 
**Temporary Generation Capacity**

Dear Executive Officer Irizarry:

On February 26, 2025, GeneraPR, LLC ("Genera") filed with the Puerto Rico Energy Bureau Public 
Utilities Regulatory Board (“PREB”) an Application for Accelerated Approval of Emergency 
Generation Capacity Solutions ("Application").

After reviewing the Application, PREB issued a Resolution and Order on February 27, 2025 
(“Order”), granting LUMA until March 6, 2025, to state its position regarding Genera’s request and, 
specifically, the need for temporary power generation capacity. The Energy Bureau also ordered 
Genera to provide LUMA immediately with any necessary information to comply with its Order.

To comply with PREB’s Order, LUMA will be providing PREB with a response as it relates to 
generation capacity. As to the feasibility of the Application, LUMA expects Genera to schedule a 
meeting to coordinate matters related to the corresponding power generation system studies and 
facilities assessment, as these also relate to the upcoming plant retirement schedule and the 
summer reliability assessment.

Please contact us at your earliest convenience to schedule the meeting and comply with PREB’s 
Order.

Sincerely,

Raphael Gignac (Mar 6, 2025 07:24 AST)

Vice President System Operations
